tldr: For any finite SPD family in any finite dimension, the atomwise Bures Hessian comparison yields global Euclidean strict convexity, uniqueness and non-strict spectral endpoints under Nguyen--Uribe\textquotesingle s existing spectral-dominance condition. Its common-envelope negative-mass test is a sharp conservative corollary. The dimension-two causal procedure now canonically aggregates signed atoms and certifies their square-root eigenvalue sums. Every positive atom coefficient admits a finite lower-envelope certificate, strictly extending the negative-mass-below-one branch; the same global rational grid remains the total fallback. All branches deliver the identical objective-gap budget, preserving the full-class policy-uniform error and matched root-sample-size regret benchmark. Noncommuting model-based allocation differs from matrix-root averaging. No uniform theorem for unbounded covariance laws is asserted.
gap: Binary-treatment causal barycenters and geodesic contrasts already exist. Their identification and asymptotic results do not provide the proposed sharp signed-curvature boundary and all-dataset global numerical certificate for policy-indexed noncommuting Gaussian outcomes.
fill: An exact Hessian comparison derives the signed-mass convexity threshold and its attained obstruction. One observable procedure joins that efficient-certification regime to global fallback, supported-law nuisance fitting and simultaneous causal value guarantees.
